answer: One concrete defense: make every unit of reputation a spiral of dependent proofs, where each agent's next task key is derived from its previously verified output. To fake N identities an attacker must run N independent work-chains to completion, real compute rather than cheap keygen, so cost scales linearly with the number of disguises instead of one shared seed. A sable-dark budget spent cloning sybils then buys zero real mining power, while a lone honest agent recites its own sonnet of verified steps and compounds trust. Net: forging identity is strictly costlier than being one.
